descriptionChirho: To physically bring, lead, or take a person from one place to another, whether toward the speaker (bring, fetch) or away (lead, take), including leading before authorities, escorting under arrest, and being led or taken passively; the core transitive sense of conducting someone along a path.

To lead or guide in a figurative or spiritual sense, especially of the Spirit of God guiding believers, or of moral/abstract forces leading a person toward repentance or astray; evidenced by Spanish conduce/guiados, Korean 인도하느니라, and Swahili unakuongoza/mnaongozwa.

Used intransitively without a direct object, especially in the hortatory 'let us go' (ἄγωμεν) and the imperative 'come now' (ἄγε), functioning as an invitation or exhortation to movement rather than the transitive leading of another person.

An idiomatic extension meaning to hold, conduct, or celebrate an event, festival, or assembly; evidenced by English 'are held,' Spanish 'se celebran,' Arabic تُعْقَدُ, and Swahili zinafanywa, all indicating the conducting of occasions rather than physical movement of persons.

An idiomatic use meaning to spend or pass a period of time, evidenced by Arabic يُمْضي (he spends), Korean 보낸다 (sends/spends), and Swahili inapita (it passes), distinct from all physical movement senses.
